Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is our latest redline of the Order Form (Fenixa_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and the pricing schedule we discussed (Pricing_Schedule_FENX.xlsx). A few quick items we want to confirm before we hand this to Legal/Finance for execution:

- Minimum commit: we proposed $75k in the redline as a path to get to a 12-month committed discount. Please confirm if you can accept $75k or need the original $100k.
- Net terms: our standard request is Net 30; Ben mentioned we can discuss Net 45 for enterprise accounts—what does procurement prefer?
- Billing entity & tax evidence: please confirm the Fenixa billing entity and provide VAT / tax ID or PO template so Finance can map invoices to the correct legal entity.
- Invoicing cadence: we proposed monthly invoicing; flagged a note on proration for activation.

Goal: if the above looks OK we’ll route the redline to Legal + Finance and send an execution-ready copy to you by early next week. If you’d prefer a short call to close open items, happy to schedule 30 minutes.

Attachments: Fenixa_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf, Pricing_Schedule_FENX.xlsx

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fenixa - Order form commercial terms: pricing + invoicing notes

Alyssa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing your PO. A few clarifications from our side that should help speed procurement/finance review:

1) Minimum commit: we are comfortable moving the committed annual spend to $75,000 (instead of $100,000) provided Fenixa agrees to the same usage tiers in Section 2 of the Pricing Schedule. That reduction reflects our desire to close this within Q3.

2) Net terms: we can accept Net 45 for the first year for deal DA-FENX-0042 if Fenixa can commit to an upfront activation invoice (month 1) paid Net 30. This splits risk and keeps cashflow predictable. If procurement can confirm Net 30 across the board, we will prefer that but can be flexible.

3) Taxes / withholding: standard approach is customer-responsible for local withholding; Redwood issues gross invoices and can provide evidence (W-8/W-9 for US, EU VAT registration for EU billing entity). For Brazil specifically, we will need to understand the applicable withholding rate and whether Fenixa can remit direct or expects Redwood to gross up. We can accept language that places withholding responsibility on the customer, with an option to gross up if required — Legal will need to review specific redline language.

4) Billing entity: please indicate whether invoices should go to Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) or Redwood EU GmbH for EU invoices — our finance team needs that mapping before we finalize.

Action items:
- Kimber: can Legal/Finance prepare a clean execution copy with the accepted $75k and the Net 45 / activation Net 30 compromise (or mark Net 30 as preferred if Fenixa confirms)?
- Marissa: please confirm whether Finance can accept Net 45 on a case-by-case basis and whether any additional credit checks are required.

If you prefer we can lock the commercials and then have Legal exchange the final Order Form via DocuSign.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fenixa - Order form commercial terms: pricing + invoicing notes

Team / Alyssa —

Finance & Legal checked the redline and summary. High-level:

- Minimum commit: Finance will accept $75k for this initial order form. Please ensure the Pricing Schedule includes the agreed tier definitions and overage rates.
- Net terms: Finance is OK to accept Net 45 given Ben's activation-invoice compromise, provided we receive a PO referencing the Deal ID (FNX-2027-0042) and standard credit checks are clear (we will run a quick credit desk review).
- Tax evidence: before final execution we need one of the following from Fenixa: W-8/W-9 (US/non-US), EU VAT ID (if EU entity), and for Brazil a local tax residency certificate or proof of withholding mechanism. This is standard for invoicing to avoid being assessed by local authorities.
- Billing entity: Redwood prefers to invoice via Redwood Inference, Inc. for this deal (US entity). If Fenixa requires EU billing, please confirm the EU entity and we will route future invoices accordingly.

I uploaded an execution-ready PDF with our standard payment instructions and the redline accepted where noted (OrderForm_execution_copy.pdf). Next steps:
- Alyssa / Procurement: provide PO (use our Deal ID in the PO), indicate billing entity preference, and attach tax IDs/documents.
- Once PO & tax docs are received, Finance will issue the first invoice (activation) and route subsequent monthly invoices.

If Fenixa wants an adjusted clause around withholding (e.g., customer remits withholding and provides certificate within 30 days), Legal can draft a short exhibit. Otherwise, our standard approach is customer pays withholding and provides evidence.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Finance & Ops
marissa_cole@redwood.com
